faq: Q1: What are Zewa Feeds Dried BSF Larvae made from?

Zewa Feeds Dried BSF Larvae contain 100% whole Black Soldier Fly larvae (Hermetia illucens) with no additives, binders, or preservatives. Each larva is microwave-dried at peak maturity to lock in 40% protein and 30% natural fat — one of the cleanest protein sources available for ornamental fish.

Zewa Feeds Dried BSF Larvae suit medium-to-large carnivorous and omnivorous ornamental fish including Arowana, Oscar, Flowerhorn, Red Tail Catfish, Discus, Carp, Goldfish, and Alligator Gar. The 2–3 cm whole-larva size matches the natural prey profile of these species.

All freshwater ornamental shrimps including Cherry, Blue Velvet and Snowball (Neocaridina), Crystal Red and Crystal Black (Caridina), plus Amano, Tiger, and Ghost Shrimp. One formula covers the shared mineral and protein needs of all dwarf shrimp species.

Their digestive systems are immature at first feeding, mouth gape is extremely small, and survival through the first 30 days is largely determined by feed quality and particle size. Generic adult feeds are unsuitable — too large, too hard, and nutritionally misbalanced.

The three-stage system matches particle size to mouth gape as fry grow: H1 (0.175–0.3 mm) from first feeding, H2 (0.3–0.5 mm) from 2–3 weeks, and H3 (0.5–0.7 mm) from 4–6 weeks. All three share an identical 48% crude protein formulation with omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids for brain, eye, and nervous system development, plus spirulina to initiate early colour expression.
Suitable for all ornamental fish hatcheries including guppy, tetra, cichlid, betta, barb, and arowana. Each stage available in 1 kg.

faq: Q1: Which Hatch'E stage should I start with?

Start with H1 (0.175–0.3 mm) at first feeding, typically 48–72 hours post-hatch once the yolk sac is absorbed. This is the smallest particle size and is calibrated for minimum larval mouth gape. Feed 4–6 small amounts daily.
Q2: When do I move from H1 to H2 to H3?

Move from H1 to H2 (0.3–0.5 mm) at approximately 2–3 weeks post-hatch, and from H2 to H3 (0.5–0.7 mm) at approximately 4–6 weeks. Exact timing varies by species — fast-growing cichlids graduate sooner, while smaller species such as tetras stay on each stage longer. Transition when fry visibly handle the current size with ease.
Q3: Can I skip a stage and go straight from H1 to H3?

This is not recommended. Each particle size matches mouth gape at a specific growth stage. Skipping H2 means offering particles too large for 2–3 week old fry, which causes underfeeding during a critical growth window and reduces survival rates.
Q4: What do I feed after Hatch'E H3?

Graduate to an adult species-specific Zewa feed once fry comfortably consume the H3 particle. Typical transitions are Guppy Bites G2 (0.3–0.6 mm), Tetra Pellets F2 (0.4–0.6 mm), Betta Bites F3 (0.6–0.8 mm), or Micro Pellets M3 (0.5–1 mm) for mixed community grow-out.
Q5: Is the formulation different between H1, H2 and H3?

No. All three stages share an identical 48% insect protein formulation, omega enrichment, ingredient list, and vitamin-mineral matrix. Only the particle size differs, which is what allows a consistent nutritional profile across the entire larval and juvenile growth period.
